# History of Neutrino Telescopes {#history}

## A telescope inside nature {#markovs-idea}

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
![](../neutrino-telescopes-2026/media/history/markov-lectern-author.gif){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 420px;" fig-alt="Moisei Markov speaking at a lectern."}

::: {.media-caption}
Moisei Alexandrovich Markov.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
**A large target already exists in nature.**

- Let us lower light sensors deep into a lake or sea.
- Once in a while a neutrino hits a nucleus and produces a charged particle.
- The particle glows in the water, and from this light we reconstruct its path.

::: {.media-caption}
M. A. Markov, Rochester conference, 1960, p. 578.
:::
:::
:::::

## DUMAND: the first attempt in the ocean {#dumand}

:::::: {.panel-tabset}

### People and a dream

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="58%"}
![](../neutrino-telescopes-2026/media/history/dumand-1976.jpg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 420px;" fig-alt="John Learned at the blackboard, Jed Hirota seated at left and Dick Davisson seated at right, DUMAND 1976 workshop."}

::: {.media-caption}
DUMAND workshop, 1976. John Learned at the board; Jed Hirota (left), Dick Davisson (right).
Photo: Anatoly Petrukhin, via IceCube.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="38%"}
**Deep Underwater Muon And Neutrino Detector**

- Reines, Learned and colleagues conceived an array in the ocean off Hawaii.
- Almost 5 km deep: all the engineering had to be invented from scratch.
- 1987: a prototype string, lowered from a ship, saw muons in the deep ocean.
:::
:::::

### 1979: Khabarovsk and Baikal

**Summer 1979: the DUMAND workshop meets in Khabarovsk and at Lake Baikal.**

- Chudakov, Berezinsky, Bezrukov, Dolgoshein, Petrukhin and Zheleznykh plan the deep-ocean telescope together with the American team.
- **December 1979:** Soviet troops enter Afghanistan.
- **1980:** the American side ends the cooperation.

> “…if perchance they included Russians it would be found that no funding was available.”

Arthur Roberts, DUMAND

::: {.takeaway}
1980: Chudakov proposes to build a “Russian DUMAND” at Lake Baikal.
:::

::: {.media-caption}
C. Spiering, *Eur. Phys. J. H* **37**, 515 (2012), [arXiv:1207.4952](https://arxiv.org/abs/1207.4952), section 4.1;
A. Roberts, *Rev. Mod. Phys.* **64**, 259 (1992).
:::

### December 1993

[4800 m below the Pacific. Nearly 500 atmospheres.]{style="font-size: 1.3em; font-weight: 700;"}

- The first string is connected on the sea floor. It sees muons.
- Over a hundred penetrators lead cables into the pressure housings. **One is flawed.**
- Seawater seeps in. **About ten hours later: a short circuit.**
- A fuse fails to clear it. The shore loses contact.
- **January 1994:** an acoustic signal releases the string from the sea floor.
- **1995: support ends.** The array is never built.

::: {.takeaway}
In the deep ocean, one connector can decide the fate of an experiment.
:::

::: {.media-caption}
DUMAND Collaboration, [astro-ph/9412019](https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/9412019);
C. Spiering, *Eur. Phys. J. H* **37**, 515 (2012), [arXiv:1207.4952](https://arxiv.org/abs/1207.4952).
:::

## Lake Baikal: the ice becomes a platform {#baikal}

:::::: {.panel-tabset}

### Why Baikal?

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="57%"}
![](../neutrino-telescopes-2026/media/history/baikal-winter-2005.jpg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 420px;" fig-alt="Winter work at Lake Baikal, 2005."}

::: {.media-caption}
Winter expedition, 2005. [DLNP JINR archive](https://dlnp.jinr.ru/chronograph/75/3258).
:::
:::
::: {.column width="39%"}
**Alexander Chudakov proposed the site.**

- Deep, clear water close to shore.
- In winter the lake is covered with ice. It is a ready-made platform: strings are lowered straight from the ice.
- From 1980 Grigory Domogatsky led the Baikal neutrino programme.
:::
:::::

### Three strings

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="52%"}
![](media/figures/nt36-side.svg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 580px;" fig-alt="Side view of NT-36: three strings with six pairs of optical modules each, hanging from an umbrella frame at a depth of 1.1 km."}
:::
::: {.column width="44%"}
**NT-36, April 1993**

- 3 strings, 36 modules.
- The modules work in pairs: a signal counts if both PMTs fire within 15 ns.
- Depth 1.1 km.

> “Congratulations for winning the 3-string race!”

John Learned to Christian Spiering
:::
:::::

::: {.media-caption}
Schematic after [Baikal Collaboration, astro-ph/9601161](https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/9601161), section 2 and Fig. 1 · pair orientation: the 1994 configuration.
:::

### First neutrinos

```{=html}
<div class="timing" style="font-size: 1em; grid-template-columns: 9rem 1fr;">
<span class="time">1980–84</span><span>A laboratory, site studies, the first strings</span>
<span class="time">1993–94</span><span>NT36: the first neutrino candidates</span>
<span class="time">1996</span><span>NT96: a clear signal of upward-going neutrinos</span>
<span class="time">1998</span><span>NT200: 192 optical modules</span>
</div>
```

::: {.takeaway}
Atmospheric neutrinos proved it: Markov's method works.
:::

::: {.media-caption}
C. Spiering, historical review (2024); [detector paper](https://cds.cern.ch/record/323330).

## Towards a cubic kilometre {#cubic-kilometre}

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="57%"}
![](../neutrino-telescopes-2026/media/history/icecube-last-dom-2010.jpg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 480px;" fig-alt="Deployment of the final IceCube optical module in December 2010."}

::: {.media-caption}
Final optical module, December 2010. IceCube/NSF.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="39%"}
**Antarctica, the ice of the South Pole**

- **AMANDA:** Halzen, Learned, Price, Morse, Barwick and colleagues try the polar ice.
- Near the surface the ice is full of bubbles, and light scatters strongly. Deeper down the bubbles disappear.
- **1999:** the cubic-kilometre proposal.
- **2010:** the last of 86 IceCube strings.
- **2013:** a flux of astrophysical neutrinos is discovered.
:::
:::::
